creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`muster daemons` fails whenever no window answers, though it is the one verb about the machine rather than a window. The CLI sends `ReadDaemons` to the window, and `windowless::can_answer` does not let this machine's daemon answer it in the window's place, as it does for `muster window` and the pane verbs.

Seen on 2026-10-26: macOS paused the app when the system ran out of memory, so its command socket took connections and never answered. `muster window` fell back to the daemon and worked. `muster daemons` refused with "no Muster window is listening", then listed what still works without a window and said "everything else is about what a window shows or how it lays out its tabs", which is not true of this verb.

A hung or quit window is when this verb is most useful: it says which daemons are alive and what they hold before anyone decides what to restart. The daemons a window started are written down under `~/.muster/state/daemons/`, so the CLI could dial each socket itself. That answer would cover this machine only, since a remote machine's daemon is known to the window that attached it.

At minimum, the refusal should stop saying that every other verb is about a window.
title: `muster daemons` fails when the window does not answer
